situation: Near Ngaoundéré, on the Adamawa Plateau, the Vina River falls over a cliff of hard rock: the Vina Falls. The water is fast, white and noisy, and the valley sides are steep.
Bouba compares it with the wide, slow Benue at Garoua. He wonders why rivers in the hills look so different from rivers on the plains.
sitQA: What is the problem raised in the situation above?
The problem is that Bouba does not understand why rivers in the hills are different from rivers on the plains.
Describe the Vina River at the falls.
The water is fast, white and noisy, and it falls over a cliff of hard rock between steep valley sides.
How can waterfalls help the people of a region?
They attract tourists, and some of them can be used to produce hydroelectricity.
end.justification: This lesson will help us to understand the young, powerful stage of a river and the landforms it creates.

qa.q: Give three characteristics of the upper course.
qa.a: The gradient is steep, the channel is narrow and shallow, and the water flows fast and turbulently over large, angular rocks.

qa.q: What is the main process in the upper course?
qa.a: The main process is vertical erosion: the river cuts down into its bed by hydraulic action and abrasion.

sum.title: I. Main Characteristics and Processes
sum.intro: The upper course is the youthful stage of the river, near its source:
items: – Fast, turbulent flow with white water.
– Hydraulic action and abrasion are very active.
– Large rocks are rolled along the bed during floods.

qa.q: How is a V-shaped valley formed?
qa.a: The river cuts down into its bed. Weathering and rain wear back the valley sides, and the loose material slides into the river. This gives steep sides in a V shape.

qa.title: Question 2
qa.q: Why does a young river wind between interlocking spurs?
qa.a: The young river cannot cut through the hard spurs, so it flows around them. The spurs lock into each other like the teeth of a zip.

qa.title: Question 3
qa.q: Explain how a waterfall is formed.
qa.a: The river flows over hard rock onto soft rock. The soft rock is eroded faster, which forms a step. The falling water digs a plunge pool and undercuts the hard rock, which collapses.

qa.q: How does a gorge form below a waterfall?
qa.a: The waterfall slowly moves back upstream as the hard rock collapses again and again. It leaves a deep, narrow valley with steep sides: a gorge.

qa.q: What are rapids, cataracts and potholes?
qa.a: Rapids are parts of a river with fast, rough water over rocks; big rapids are cataracts. Potholes are round holes drilled in the bed by stones turned by the water.

sum.title: II. Landforms of the Upper Course
sum.intro: Vertical erosion forms the following landforms:
items: The river cuts down, and the valley sides are worn back, forming a narrow valley with steep sides in a V shape.
The river winds around spurs of hard rock that lock into each other like the teeth of a zip.
A waterfall forms where the river flows from hard rock onto soft rock. It retreats upstream and leaves a gorge. Examples: Vina and Tello Falls (Adamawa), Kola Gorges (near Guider).
– Rapids: fast, rough water over rocks; large rapids are cataracts.
– Potholes: round holes drilled in the rocky bed by swirling stones.

evaluation: What is the main process in the upper course?
Vertical erosion is the main process.
Why does a waterfall retreat upstream?
The water undercuts the hard rock, which collapses again and again, so the fall moves back.
Give one example of a waterfall in Cameroon.
The Vina Falls near Ngaoundéré (also the Tello, Ekom-Nkam or Lobé Falls).
remediation: The upper course has a ______ gradient.
The valley of the upper course is ______-shaped.
The deep hole at the foot of a waterfall is a ______ pool.
A narrow valley left by a retreating waterfall is a ______.
Round holes in a river bed are ______.
end.remediationAnswers: 1. steep 2. V 3. plunge 4. gorge 5. potholes 6. cataracts
end.homework: Stand on the Benue Bridge in Garoua or look at a photo of it. Draw the river and its bends, and mark where the water seems fastest.
end.homeworkTag: This prepares Lesson 20: The Middle Course of a River.
teacherNote: Local examples checked: Vina Falls and Tello Falls near Ngaoundéré; Kola Gorges near Guider (North Region); Ekom-Nkam Falls (Littoral/West); Lobé Falls near Kribi fall directly into the sea.
The syllabus notions include cataracts: large rapids or waterfalls on big rivers (e.g. the cataracts of the Nile).
references: National Geography Syllabus (MINESEC), Form 4 — Denudation Processes, Landforms and Impacts on Man.
